Q3698094.summary: This gold Latin cross, about 22.5 cm high, with gently flaring arms, is studded with a symmetrical pattern of blue and white stones and pearls set in beaded collars, and hung with six gold pendants on fine chains. A masterpiece of Lombard goldsmiths' work, it honours the Cross of Christ as a jewelled sign of victory rather than as an instrument of suffering.
facts: It is traditionally associated with the Lombard king Agilulf (d. 616), husband of Queen Theodelinda, and may have hung from a royal crown.
Its overall form and the arrangement of six pendants are Byzantine in style, while the decoration shows 'barbarian' influence, suggesting it was made within the Lombard kingdom.
Q3698094.notes: No figure of Christ is visible in the available photograph: the cross is decorated with gems and pearls. Italian Wikipedia and Wikidata state that it bears representations of Christ, archangels and apostles (presumably on engraved stones), but this could not be confirmed, so the entry is kept as uncertain; if the claim cannot be substantiated it should be removed as a non-figural cross. The Commons file description wrongly calls it a 'diptych of Gregory the Great'.

Q109422137.summary: This narrow ivory strip tells the night of Christ's betrayal in three scenes. At the top a servant-girl points accusingly at Peter in the courtyard of the high priest; in the middle Peter sits weeping, head in hand, with the cock perched before him; at the bottom the haloed Christ is led away between soldiers toward Pilate. The juxtaposition sets Peter's human weakness beside Christ's calm acceptance of his Passion.
facts: It is a side panel from a five-part ivory leaf, of the kind assembled around a larger central plaque.
The Louvre bought it in 1895 from the collector Charles Mannheim.
The cock recalls Christ's prophecy that Peter would deny him three times before the cock crowed.
Q109422137.notes: The Louvre identifies the lowest scene as Christ led to Pilate (Wikidata/Commons title: 'arrest of Christ'). Date and Ravenna attribution are given by the Louvre with a query, on stylistic grounds.
Q109422137.original_title: Plaque latérale d'un feuillet en cinq parties : Le Reniement de saint Pierre ; le Christ emmené chez Pilate
